messages.subject: Covariates in MR model
parts:
Hello,

I am using an MRDS point independence model to analyze an io line transect survey. One of the available covariates is "species identification certainty", which is basically how sure the observers were of the species identity on a scale of 1 (certain) to 3 (very uncertain). Inclusion of this covariate as a factor does improve the MR model. However I am uncertain if it is appropriate to do so, because it seems somewhat tautological. If an observer is uncertain of species identification, it probably means that the sighting was a difficult one, which makes it less likely to be duplicated by the other team. In effect the observer is somewhat subjectively assessing the probability of duplication.

There is also the issue that the two observer teams often do not agree on the identification certainty, but the same problem exists for other covariates (e.g. cluster size) as well.

So my question is: is it appropriate to use a subjective judgement of sighting quality like this in an MR model, or should one stick to less subjective covariates such as weather condition, visibility etc.

Thanks in advance,

Daniel Pike.
